Done. I created /workspace/proxy.ts implementing the request-id header and pathname logging.

Key point: this project runs Next.js 16 (^16.4.0-canary.52), where middleware.js/middleware.ts is deprecated and renamed to proxy.js/proxy.ts per the bundled docs. So the file uses the new proxy convention rather than the old middleware export.

What the file does:
- Generates a unique id per request via randomUUID().
- Logs [proxy] <pathname> to the console using request.nextUrl.pathname.
- Sets X-Request-Id on the response (response.headers.set('X-Request-Id', requestId)).
- Also forwards the same id as a request header (x-request-id) upstream via NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } }), following the documented API (and the doc's warning to use request: { headers }, not the top-level headers).
- A matcher excludes _next/static, _next/image, and favicon.ico so the header/logging doesn't run on static internals.

Verification:
- npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0.
- npm run build → exit 0; build output lists ƒ Proxy (Middleware).
- npm run start + two curl requests to /:
  - Response headers include x-request-id: 14c99297-… and x-request-id: 98fea6d9-… — present and unique per request.
  - Server stdout shows [proxy] / twice — pathname logging confirmed.
